h: פָּרָשַׁת פָּרָה, מַאֲמָר ו׳ Parshas Parah — Maamar Vav

p: In the Pesikta for Parah (section 14, siman 16):
וְאָסַף אִישׁ טָהוֹר אֵת אֵפֶר הַפָּרָה
"'And a pure man shall gather the ashes of the parah'
this is the Holy One, blessed be He,
of Whom it is written, 'And He will raise,' etc.,
'and He will gather the dispersed of Yisrael' (Yeshayah 11:12).
'Man' — this is the Holy One, blessed be He,
דִּכְתִיב [שְׁמוֹת טו, ג] ה׳ אִישׁ מִלְחָמָה.
as it is written (Shemos 15:3), 'Hashem is a Man of war.'
'Pure' — this is the Holy One, blessed be He:
these are the exiles of Yisrael," etc.;
And we must understand, according to this exposition,
מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר אַחַר כָּךְ [בְּמִדְבַּר שָׁם, י]
"And the one who gathers the ashes of the parah shall wash
But the matter is, as it is written (Yeshayah 63:1–3):
"Who is this who comes from Edom," etc.,
and of the peoples there was no man with Me," etc.,
"and their lifeblood spattered on My garments,
and I have stained all My clothing."
"and of the peoples there was no man with Me"?
Rather, at that time there will be the refinement,
and "there will be no survivor of the house of Esav,"
אֲשֶׁר לֹא עָלָה עָלֶיהָ עוֹל [בְּמִדְבַּר שָׁם, ב]
"upon which no yoke has come" (Bamidbar ibid. 2) —
"and it was given over to the burning of fire"
And the Holy One, blessed be He, does not rejoice
at the downfall of the wicked,
"The work of My hands is drowning in the sea,
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וּמֵעַמִּים אֵין אִישׁ אִתִּי
And this is what it says, "and of the peoples there was no man with Me" —
that there will be no survivor, etc.;
"and their lifeblood spattered on My garments,
and I have stained all My clothing" —
for then it will be necessary, so to speak,
For the King is in ten garments,
for the creation of the world,
and among them are the words of Torah,
which are the conduct of things in this world.
וּבִפְסִיקְתָּא (שׂוֹשׂ אָשִׂישׂ פָּרָשָׁה לז סִימָן, ב)
And in the Pesikta (Sos Asis, section 37, siman 2)
it counts as the last garment:
"For Torah will go forth from Me,"
"A new Torah will go forth from Me —
a renewal of Torah will go forth from Me";
of the words of Torah will be new garments,
"The Torah a person learns in this world
הֶבֶל הוּא לִפְנֵי תּוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ
is vanity before the Torah of Mashiach."
כָּל הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁאַתְּ לָמֵד בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
"All the Torah you learn in this world
הֶבֶל הוּא לִפְנֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
is vanity before the Torah of the World to Come."
That is, then there will be
another garment for the words of Torah.
And in truth, regarding the entire feast of the future,
כָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ״ם (הִלְכוֹת תְּשׁוּבָה פֶּרֶק ח הֲלָכָה ד)
that it is by way of parable
but the Rambam's view is stated explicitly
that the feast and the preserved wine
which have not yet been revealed
and will be revealed in the future;
And then "a new Torah will go forth from Me,"
and there will be a renewed garment in the words of Torah,
and all the Torah of this world
הֶבֶל הוּא לִפְנֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
is vanity before the Torah of the World to Come.
And this is what it says, "and I have stained all My clothing" —
that then there will be need
for washing all the garments, so to speak.
And indeed we find in the holy Zohar
under the soles of your feet" —
that of all the wicked something will remain,
so that they will be ashes under the feet of the tzaddikim;
but of Edom it is written,
"and there will be no survivor," etc.,
that of it and its kelipah
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר וְיֵז נִצְחָם עַל בְּגָדַי
And of this it says, "and their lifeblood spattered on My garments,
and I have stained all My clothing."
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר וְכִבֶּס הָאוֹסֵף וְגוֹמֵר
And of this it says, "And the one who gathers shall wash," etc. —
that He will need, so to speak,
and "a renewal of Torah will go forth from Me,"
"From His right hand, a fiery law for them,"
that at first He wished to create the world
and He saw that it would not endure,
so He joined the attribute of mercy to the attribute of judgment.
And this is why the Torah is called fire,
and nevertheless it is "from His right hand,"
for He joined the attribute of mercy to the attribute of judgment —
that is, in the garment of the words of Torah
for the creation of the world.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב רו, ב)
And this is what they said in the holy Zohar (II 206b):
"For the Torah was given from two sides,
as it is written, 'From His right hand, a fiery law for them' —
and this is as mentioned above.
And in the future the words of Torah will be
as it first arose in thought, with the attribute of judgment,
that in the future the halachah will follow Beis Shammai,
which is the attribute of gevurah
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רמה, א).
(as is written in the Zohar III 245a).
וְאוֹרַיְיתָא וְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא חַד הוּא
And "the Torah and the Holy One, blessed be He, are one,"
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב ס, א)
as they said in the holy Zohar (II 60a):
וְאוֹלִיפְנָא דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא תּוֹרָה אִיקְרֵי
"And we have learned that the Holy One, blessed be He, is called Torah,
וְאֵין תּוֹרָה אֶלָּא קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וְכוּ׳
and Torah is nothing but the Holy One, blessed be He," etc.
And this is "and I have stained all My clothing,"
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר וְכִבֶּס הָאוֹסֵף וְגוֹמֵר
and of this it says, "And the one who gathers shall wash," etc.,
which is expounded about the Holy One, blessed be He,
Who gathers and assembles the dispersed of Yisrael,
And on Shabbos, which is a semblance of the World to Come
and one-sixtieth of the World to Come
resembling the Torah of the World to Come.

paragraphs.text: Pesikta Rabbasi 14:16, Parah — “A pure man shall gather all the ashes of the heifer: this is the Holy One, blessed be He, of whom it is written, He shall raise a banner to the nations and gather Israel's dispersed. A man is the Holy One, blessed be He, for Hashem is a man of war. Pure is the Holy One, blessed be He, pure of eyes from seeing evil. The heifer's ashes are Israel's exiles. He shall place them outside the camp in a pure place: this is Jerusalem, which is pure.”

paragraphs.text: Yalkut Shimoni, Yeshayahu, remez 506:1 — “Israel are called bride in ten places. ... Correspondingly the Holy One, blessed be He, wore ten garments. The first, worn when He created the world, was majesty and splendor: You clothed Yourself in majesty and splendor. The second, to exact payment from the generation of the Flood, was exaltation: Hashem reigns; He clothed Himself in exaltation. The third, to give Torah to Israel, was strength: Hashem clothed Himself in strength and girded Himself. The fourth, to exact payment from Bavel, was snow: His garment was white as snow. The fifth, to exact payment from Madai, was vengeance: He wore garments of vengeance as clothing, and wrapped Himself in zeal as a cloak—these are two. The seventh, to exact payment from Yavan, was righteousness: He wore righteousness as a breastplate, and a helmet of salvation upon His head—these are two. The ninth, to exact payment from the fourth kingdom, Edom: Why is Your clothing red? The tenth, to exact payment from Gog and Magog, is glorious: This One, glorious in His clothing. The congregation of Israel said: Master of the world, of all the garments You have worn, none is as beautiful as this.” The Yalkut explicitly counts ten. This differs from the seven-garment sequence in Pesikta Rabbasi 37. In this witness the red garment against Edom is ninth, and the glorious garment against Gog and Magog is tenth. Rav Tzadok joins the ten-garment tradition with the ten sefiros; the two Midrashic enumerations should retain their own order.

paragraphs.text: Pesikta Rabbasi 37:2, Sos asis — “The Holy One, blessed be He, wore seven garments from the creation of the world until He takes judgment upon wicked Edom: when He created the world, majesty and splendor; at the sea, exaltation; when He gave Torah, strength; against the Chaldeans, vengeance; when He forgives Israel, white; when Mashiach appears, righteousness; and a red garment, Why is Your clothing red? This is the judgment upon Edom.” This digital witness enumerates seven garments. Rav Tzadok elsewhere explicitly reports a Yalkut reading of ten garments; that reported variant should be distinguished from this witness. The final red garment is present in both discussions.

paragraphs.text: Vayikra Rabbah 13:3 — “Rabbi Avin bar Kahana said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said, A new Torah shall go forth from Me—a renewal of Torah shall go forth from Me. Rabbi Berechyah said in Rabbi Yitzchak's name: The Holy One, blessed be He, will make a feast for His righteous servants in the future.” The Midrash discusses the future feast and the question of its mode of slaughter. Rav Tzadok focuses on the words a renewal of Torah.

paragraphs.text: Kohelet Rabbah 2:1 — “Rabbi Chizkiyah said in Rabbi Simon bar Zavdi's name: All the Torah you learn in this world is insubstantial beside the Torah of the World to Come. In this world a person learns Torah and forgets; in the future it is written, I shall place My Torah within them.” The Midrash explains its comparison through the disappearance of forgetting. It does not dismiss the present obligation or worth of Torah study.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Arizal, Sha'ar HaHakdamos, Introductions 1 — “Occupying oneself with the Torah in its plain sense, the Torah of this world, which is vanity before the Torah of Mashiach and the Torah of the World to Come.” The Arizal applies the same midrash to the plain garment of the present Torah. Rav Tzadok says this garment will one day be washed and renewed.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Rabbi Mordechai Yosef Leiner, Mei HaShiloachI, Chukas 2 — “In the future the blessed God will reveal His glory to Israel without any garment. Even now this life is found in Israel's depths, but it is not manifest except through garments. The garments are Torah and commandments, for one can reach the depth of God's will only through Torah and commandments. Take for yourself a cow: this is life, as is known; for the present they were commanded that life be within garments, namely Torah and commandments.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: Mei HaShiloach distinguishes the concealed life from the Torah and commandments through which it is presently reached. It sharpens Rav Tzadok's garment language: future disclosure develops a life already present, while its present form remains Torah and mitzvos.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 237a–b, Pekudei 37, s.v. Amar lei — “The cow included the four kingdoms: red is Bavel, perfect is Madai, without blemish is Yavan, and upon which no yoke came is Edom. ... Who can bring pure from impure? Here the pure comes from the impure: at first it was impure, but now judgment was performed upon it, it was given to burning fire and made dust. ... All who work with it become impure. After it becomes ash, it imparts impurity until it is gathered and removed: The gatherer shall wash ... and is impure. Why ash? You shall tread upon the wicked, for they shall be ash beneath the soles of your feet. When water is placed upon that ash, then it is pure from impure.” The Zohar connects the heifer, the kingdoms, ash, and purification through judgment. Rav Tzadok develops a further distinction between the residue of the other wicked and Edom's complete disappearance.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 12:15 — “Hashem God: This is compared to a king with empty cups. He said: If I put hot liquid into them, they will split; cold liquid, and they will contract. What did the king do? He mixed hot and cold and put it into them, and they endured. So the Holy One, blessed be He, said: If I create the world with mercy alone, sins will abound; with judgment alone, how can the world endure? Rather, I create it with judgment and mercy; would that it endure.” The Midrash explains the combination of Divine Names through the union of judgment and mercy. Rav Tzadok applies it to the Torah's present garment.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 206b, Vayakhel 17, s.v. Trei zimnei — “At Shabbos Minchah, at the time when judgment hangs suspended toward evening, one must include the left within the right, for Torah was given from two sides: From His right, a fiery law for them—right and left. Therefore at Minchah ten verses or more suffice for the Torah reading, but not the completion of the section, for the section's completion belongs only to the right.” Rav Tzadok cites the union of right and left to explain Torah's present combination of mercy and judgment.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Hashanah 7 — “At the start of creation man was made upright, always cleaving to eternal life; this is called the attribute of judgment, for such is the conduct of the perfect tzaddikim.” This explains what the future Torah “in judgment” means. It is not harshness. It is the exacting closeness of the perfect tzaddik, as Yaakov took even mercy as judgment (Zohar I 151b).

paragraphs.text: Rabbi Shalom Buzaglo, Mikdash Melech, Zohar I 17b:3 — “Alternatively, And it endured means: Every controversy that is for the sake of Heaven is destined to endure. A heavenly voice went forth and said: These and those are the words of the living God, for Shammai's words too have a root above. Although the law does not follow them in this world, they are destined to endure in the future. As the Arizal wrote on this Mishnah, in the future, in Mashiach's time, the law will follow Beis Shammai. The words of both are abiding and true; the Holy One, blessed be He, distinguished between them and agreed to them.” Mikdash Melech explicitly transmits the future-law teaching in the Arizal's name. This verifies an early commentary witness to the attribution. Likkutei Torah, Korach, by R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, repeats it: “The Arizal explained that in the future, in the time of Mashiach, the halachah will follow Beis Shammai.” It cites the Mikdash Melech for this, however, and is not an independent witness. Agra DeKala, Korach, also reports it: “as is known to us from the holy writings of the Arizal… in the future the halachah will follow Beis Shammai.” The passage in the Arizal's own transmitted writings has not been located. The cited ZoharIII 245a establishes the schools' roots in mercy and judgment separately.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 245a, Raaya Mehemna, Pinchas 90, s.v. Amar Raaya — “The Faithful Shepherd said: Hillel and Shammai, you who came, one from the side of mercy and one from the side of judgment, which are kindness and might, the levels of Avraham and Yitzchak—you are of their stock. Gather here, you and the eighty students Hillel had, and likewise the students of Beis Shammai, for the King's feast.” The Zohar establishes the schools' roots in kindness and might. It does not itself state here that future law follows Beis Shammai; that separate claim is attributed by Rav Tzadok to the Arizal, and its witnesses are given in the preceding note.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas Shabbos 7 — “The blessing of the Shabbos day, a semblance of the World to Come, is renewal of the light of Torah of the days of Mashiach… when every heart will flow with wisdom.” This spells out what the “semblance” is. On Shabbos the heart already tastes the Torah that will one day well up from within.
